Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz, Priya Singh, Zoe Tan, Liam Rhodes, Jules Park, Anika Rao, plus a few observers on mute.

Transcript body: (timestamps approximate, transcription is imperfect)
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, let's get started. Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on, we'll run 60, 70 minutes ish. First up, quick recap on the September 22nd incident — Rafael, can you take us through the timeline?
[00:00:18] Rafael Ortiz: Sure, yeah. So on 9/22 at about 13:05 UTC a model rollout hit a bad weight matrix that caused misaligned kernel dispatches and a memory spike. Our autoscaler didn't trigger fast enough because the burst policy was constrained by the shard limits — I know that phrasing's fuzzy in the logs but the gist is we hit a combination of cold K-V cache churn plus long prefix sequences that pushed a couple of pods into OOM.
[00:00:46] Priya Singh: To add, there was also a fallback path that kicked us into a lower-capacity model variant but it wasn't set up for immediate routing, so some users saw high latency vs outright failure.
[00:01:02] Jules Park: We also saw increased tail latency from the continuous batching queue — the batching window extended because of a couple of large streaming requests. That exacerbated the queue filling.
[00:01:15] Anika Rao: From a security/compliance angle, no data exfiltration, no leakage to shared caches, all encryption keys rotated during the incident as a precaution, logs captured. We still have to tidy up the audit trail for SOC2 — there are a few missing annotations in the runbook.
[00:01:32] Maya Chen: Right. Okay, so high level we had a multi-factor failure: model artifact problem + cache coldness + autoscaler lag + routing fallback not instant. Actionable takeaway is we need a clearer playbook for rollbacks and faster fallback routing.
[00:01:45] Rafael Ortiz: Agreed. Proposed fix: create an explicit canary abort hook that, if certain memory metrics cross threshold x, immediately route traffic to safe model variant and trigger a partial drain of affected nodes.
[00:02:00] Priya Singh: Means changes to the runtime and the control plane. We need an API-level signal from the serving runtime to the router that says "drain now". The runtime already exposes memory and kv cache residency stats but we don't surface them to the routing policy today.
[00:02:16] Zoe Tan: Will product be okay with a more conservative default? Can we still offer aggressive defaults for dev/test customers? We should avoid surprising enterprise customers with drop-in higher latency.
[00:02:28] Maya Chen: Yes let's default to conservative for hosted and dedicated, and provide a knob for dev sandboxing.
[00:02:35] [00:02:36] Liam Rhodes: On the ops side, I've got a proposal: bump the Dedicated autoscale headroom from 15% to 25% during rollouts. It's a temporary policy window for 30 minutes post-rollout. That should give the scheduler time to react and avoid pod OOM.
[00:02:51] Priya Singh: We should test that in staging first; also quantify cost delta. 10% more headroom could be sizable at peak.
[00:03:03] Maya Chen: Yes, Priya do a cost estimate. But safety first for production.
[00:03:10] [00:03:11] Jules Park: Also propose pre-rollout KV cache warmup for long-lived sessions — pre-seed cache with common prefixes and hold sessions warm for X minutes. There will be complexity if the model changes token ID mapping but it's doable with a short compatibility layer.
[00:03:29] Rafael Ortiz: We have to watch for tokenization drift; if token ids remap keys could be invalid. That means the warmup step needs to run after the model artifact is pinned into serving nodes.
[00:03:42] Anika Rao: On compliance, I want to flag the audit artifacts: we need proof of the runbook changes and a table of who approved what. I can pull the raw logs but need the annotated runbook entries with time stamps.
[00:03:53] Maya Chen: Action: Anika + Liam will collate SOC2 artifacts.
[00:03:58] [00:04:00] Topic switch — Resilience playbook and runbook updates
[00:04:05] Liam Rhodes: I've circulated a draft runbook v2 — it's in the shared deck link (see notes). Main additions: explicit abort hook, autoscale headroom window, KV cache warmup, and a fallthrough routing policy that prefers older stable model variants when confidence dips.
[00:04:26] Zoe Tan: I liked the fallthrough policy but we need to define "confidence dip" — is that latency percentiles, model log-prob divergence, or memory signals?
[00:04:36] Rafael Ortiz: Start with memory and tail latency percentiles, then add model quality signals from our eval infra. We don't want to trigger rollback purely from noisy latencies.
[00:04:47] Priya Singh: Also instrument a "graceful degrade" banner for API users so product can signal temporary quality reduction vs unavailability — transparency with customers.
[00:05:00] Maya Chen: Good. Zoe, wording for public API status page?
[00:05:05] Zoe Tan: We'll prepare a template.
[00:05:10] [00:05:12] Topic switch — Tabletop drill planning
[00:05:15] Jules Park: Recommend 90-minute drill: introduce scenario (bad model artifact), execute abort hook, route traffic, communicate internally, verify logs and SOC artifacts. We'll need one person to play "customer" and one for "on-call rotation".
[00:05:32] Liam Rhodes: Prefer afternoon slot so east coast folks can attend. Week of Oct 19 looks open.
[00:05:39] Maya Chen: Set provisional date Oct 21, 14:00 PT.
[00:05:44] Jules Park: I'll draft the script and invite all SREs + product leads.
[00:05:48] [00:05:50] Topic switch — Dedicated autoscale policy changes
[00:05:53] Priya Singh: Quick note: changing headroom affects billing and reserved capacity math. For customers on Dedicated reserved capacity we need to communicate if we increase headroom because it touches their SLA and spend. For new rollouts we can opt-in.
[00:06:08] Maya Chen: So we should position it as a safety toggle that customers can enable during their model rollouts; default is off for reserved customers unless they opt in. For hosted customers we'll keep conservative default.
[00:06:21] Rafael Ortiz: The technical implementation is straightforward: autoscaler policy table plus an annotation on rollout manifests. The tricky part is UI and the console flags.
[00:06:33] Zoe Tan: I'll coordinate the UI copy; also add a changelog entry.
[00:06:38] [00:06:40] Topic switch — Compliance and SOC2 readiness
[00:06:42] Anika Rao: Audit readiness status: we have encryption coverage, KMS integration, and key rotation logs. Missing: signed approvals for the new runbook sections, and a few retention policy exceptions that need justification.
[00:06:56] Maya Chen: Who can own the signed approvals?
[00:06:58] Anika Rao: Execs — Maya, Rafael, Priya to sign off on runbook v2.
[00:07:06] Maya Chen: I'll sign. Rafael?
[00:07:08] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, will review and sign.
[00:07:10] Priya Singh: I'll check the changes for runtime impact and sign off too.
[00:07:15] [00:07:16] Topic switch — Observability and instrumentation gaps
[00:07:18] Jules Park: We need richer signals from the runtime: per-request KV cache hit/miss, dispatch memory pressure, batching window duration, and a per-model quality score emitted to the control plane.
[00:07:31] Priya Singh: We should back that with retention policy: keep high-res metrics for 7 days and aggregated for 90 days. Cost estimates needed.
[00:07:39] Maya Chen: Add to action items — Priya to estimate.
[00:07:45] [00:07:46] Misc notes and Q&A
[00:07:48] Zoe Tan: Question — do we want to change our communication plan to customers during incidents? For example, a short-running incident vs a prolonged one, and an RBC (root cause brief) cadence?
[00:07:58] Maya Chen: Yes, define a 3-point cadence: acknowledge within 15 minutes, update at 1 hour with new info, and provide a root-cause brief within 72 hours. That should be codified in the runbook.
[00:08:12] Anika Rao: We should also add an internal escalation matrix with backups for exec-level signoff.
[00:08:18] [00:08:20] Closing and recap
[00:08:22] Maya Chen: Quick recap — go over action items and owners. Liam, you lead runbook v2 drafting with Jules and Anika. Priya does autoscale tests and cost delta. Jules runs the tabletop drill and script. Anika + Liam pull SOC2 artifacts and I, Rafael, Priya will sign the runbook. Zoe prepares status page copy and changelog.
[00:08:45] Priya Singh: I'll run a stress test on staging with a synthetic workload that mimics prefix-heavy sessions and long streaming requests. Expect results by 10/14.
[00:08:55] Liam Rhodes: I'll circulate runbook v2 by 10/12.
[00:08:58] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else?
[00:09:02] Rafael Ortiz: One more tiny thing — we should look at model compilation fallbacks: if a kernel selection fails, have a hot fallback kernel precompiled. Small uptick in image size but huge safety win.
[00:09:13] Priya Singh: We can test that as a flag in the runtime.
[00:09:16] [00:09:18] End: thanks everyone. Notes: shared deck link: internal/redwood/allhands/resilience-2026-10-05 (placeholder). Post-meeting follow-up: runbook v2 draft, tabletop script, autoscale cost analysis, SOC2 artifact bundle.

Transcription notes: occasional mislabels and word substitution (K-V sometimes as K-V cache, VPC transcribed as V-P-C), filler words present.
